title: Verdier-duality exchange
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a_0,q,k_0,k)$ with
$k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a
finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and
uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and an integer $n\ge1$. Put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and choose
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ as in
[def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $X$ and $Y$ be separated finite-type
$k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Equip these schemes and morphisms with
the six-functor datum [def-sf-datum], including the constructible exceptional
inverse image $Rf^!$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]; no ambient
admissibility datum is assumed, and every such morphism is exceptionally
admissible in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility]. Let
$a_Y:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism and put
$a_X=a_Y\circ f$. Define

$$
\omega_T=Ra_T^!\Lambda_s,\qquad
D_T(K)=R\mathcal H om_T(K,\omega_T)\quad(K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)),
$$

for $T=X,Y$, where $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\Lambda_s$ is the coefficient unit [def-sf-pf]; the finite-Tor categories are those of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Then for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
D_Y(Rf_!M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_*D_X(M),
$$

natural in $M$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and
shifts.

proof.text: The coefficient unit $\Lambda_s$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$: at a finite stage it is the constant rank-one free module in degree zero, whose tensor with a degree-zero module is that module; at the integral stage its reductions are these same rank-one units, with the common Tor interval $[0,0]$; the field stages use the rationalized and common-stage units and their defining equality $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Axiom (A1) of [def-sf-datum] is imposed on the finite-Tor categories, so its right adjoint $Ra_T^!$ takes this unit to an object of $D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$, for $T=X,Y$. By [def-sf-pf] this object is $\omega_T$. The same typed axiom places $Rf_!M$ in $D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Thus every dual and every input of the tensor–Hom theorem below has its required domain. No use of Verdier biduality (A6) is made.

source.place: Step 2: verifying the parenthetical domain of N=omega_Y

proof.text:
Use axiom (A4) of [def-sf-datum] at the composable pair
$X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow {a_Y}s$ to obtain the supplied comparison
\(\alpha:Ra_{X!}=R(a_Y\circ f)_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_{Y!}Rf_!\).
For objects $K$ and $L$ in the finite-Tor categories, the three A1
adjunctions and their pasted units and counits give the natural chain
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,Rf^!Ra_Y^!L)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_!K,Ra_Y^!L)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_{Y!}Rf_!K,L)\\
&\xrightarrow{h\mapsto h\circ\alpha_K}
\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_{X!}K,L)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,Ra_X^!L).
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus Yoneda gives the mate isomorphism $Rf^!Ra_Y^!L\cong Ra_X^!L$;
this is the explicit conjugation calculation, with no appeal to the
finite-level composition theorem. Evaluating at $L=\Lambda_s$ and using
[def-sf-pf] gives
$c_f:Rf^!\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_X$.

source.place: Step 1: A4 composition comparison and its mate

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sf-tensor-hom] with the given $M$ and with $N=\omega_Y$, whose finite-Tor membership was checked in Step 1. Invert that canonical isomorphism, and follow it by the image of $c_f$ under the functor $Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,-)$. The resulting composite is
$$
D_Y(Rf_!M)=R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,Rf^!\omega_Y)
\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,\omega_X)=Rf_*D_X(M).
$$
The equalities use precisely the dualizing and Verdier-dual notation of [def-sf-pf]. Both arrows are isomorphisms, so this defines the required canonical isomorphism.

source.place: Step 2: specialize tensor–Hom and substitute the composition mate

proof.text: The tensor–Hom arrow in Step 3 has the naturality and finite-reduction, scalar-extension and shift compatibilities asserted in [lem-sf-tensor-hom]. For the second arrow, $c_f$ is independent of $M$, so bifunctoriality of internal Hom makes it natural in $M$. For a permitted coefficient comparison, apply it to the explicit unit–composition–counit Hom-adjunction chain in Step 2. Axiom (A5) of [def-sf-datum] identifies the images of those units, composition comparisons and counits with the corresponding ones after coefficient change. Substituting these three identities in that expression gives the same mate, hence the same $c_f$, after coefficient change; applying the internal-Hom comparison gives the commuting square for the second arrow. Here finite reduction is used only at finite/integral stages and scalar passage only on the domains specified by (A5). Finally, for a shift $M[r]$, the second arrow is $Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M[r],c_f)=Rf_*(R\mathcal H om_X(M,c_f)[-r])$ under the usual derived-Hom shift identification: a degree-zero map in the second variable is unchanged by shifting the first variable. Thus it has the same shift compatibility. Pasting these squares with those of the first arrow proves all asserted compatibilities of their composite.

source.place: Step 3: naturality and compatibility of the two ingredients

blueprint_update.statement:
In the setting of [def-sf-datum], let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated
finite-type morphism, with $Rf^!$ and the dualizing complexes
$\omega_X=Ra_X^!\Lambda$, $\omega_Y=Ra_Y^!\Lambda$ formed with the
constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]
(no admissibility datum is assumed; every separated finite-type morphism is
exceptionally admissible in the sense of [def-trf-admissibility]). Then for
$M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ there is a canonical isomorphism

$$
D_Y(Rf_!M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rf_*D_X(M),
$$

natural in $M$, compatible with finite reduction, scalar extension, and
shifts.

proof.text:
The operations are those of the six-functor datum of [def-sf-datum],
its projection transformation is [def-sf-pf], and the mate calculus
is that of [lem-sf-mate]; the formal core is
[fix-cor-verdier-exchange].
Step 1: $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$. By axiom (A4) and
[lem-sf-mate], the mate of the composition law [thm-sf-comp-composition]
$R(a_Y\circ f)_!\cong Ra_{Y!}Rf_!$ is the isomorphism
$Rf^!Ra_Y^!\cong Ra_X^!$, i.e. $Rf^!\omega_Y\cong\omega_X$. Step 2: apply
[lem-sf-tensor-hom] with $N=\omega_Y$ (an object of
$D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$) and substitute Step 1:

$$
D_Y(Rf_!M)=R\mathcal H om_Y(Rf_!M,\omega_Y)
\cong Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,f^!\omega_Y)
\cong Rf_*R\mathcal H om_X(M,\omega_X)=Rf_*D_X(M).
$$

Step 3: naturality and the compatibilities are those of
[lem-sf-tensor-hom] and of the mate construction of
[lem-sf-mate].

lean.statement:
theorem verdier_exchange
    (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (hl : l ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    : Assertion l Ω D hl f
lean.note: Reuses the published all-stage canonical Verdier exchange already attached to sk-thm-sf-verdier-exchange (the blueprint same_as unit). Assertion quantifies over the normalized constructible System choices for f, a_Y and a_X, and Package supplies the evaluation/projection-transposed natural isomorphisms and their signed-shift and allowed coefficient squares. These are the actual finite-Tor coefficient categories and constructible exceptional operations prescribed by SixFunctorDatum, not ambient exceptional-adjoint data. The finite-only ordinary-etale Nonempty-iso theorem is not used as an all-stage substitute. No new module, operation, or theorem is introduced.
